messages.author: b7c2064c737945ab
messages.subject: cannot start rattle. Error message: address 0xc00001c4f, cause 'memory not mapped'
parts:
Hello,

I've installed rattle on Linux. I got the following error:

> library(rattle)
Rattle: A free graphical interface for data mining with R.
Version 2.6.26 r77 Copyright (c) 2006-2013 Togaware Pty Ltd.
Type 'rattle()' to shake, rattle, and roll your data.
> rattle()
Error: attempt to apply non-function
In addition: Warning message:
In method(obj, ...) : Unknown internal child: selection

After looking at previous posts, I tried the following command but new error comes up:

>  crv$rattleUI <- "rattle_macosx.ui"
> rattle()

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0xc00001c4f, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: .Call("RS_XML_ParseTree", as.character(file), handlers, as.logical(ignoreBlanks),     as.logical(replaceEntities), as.logical(asText), as.logical(trim),     as.logical(validate), as.logical(getDTD), as.logical(isURL),     as.logical(addAttributeNamespaces), as.logical(useInternalNodes),     as.logical(isHTML), as.logical(isSchema), as.logical(fullNamespaceInfo),     as.character(encoding), as.logical(useDotNames), xinclude,     error, addFinalizer, as.integer(options), as.logical(parentFirst),     PACKAGE = "XML")
 2: xmlTreeParse(file.path(etc, "tooltips.xml"), useInternalNodes = TRUE)
 3: loadTooltips()
 4: rattle()

Possible actions:
1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
2: normal R exit
3: exit R without saving workspace
4: exit R saving workspace
Selection: 

Below is my session info:

> sessionInfo()

Platform: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (64-bit)

locale:

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: cannot start rattle. Error message: address 0xc00001c4f, cause 'memory not mapped'
parts:
Thanks for reporting the problem.

A new GUI object type got added accidentally - works just fine on Linux but the Windows libraries are old.

Please try the latest beta release (r138 or better):
> install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com")

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com
